inspiration.observed_pattern: A reusable integer sequence joins each JSON document up to JSON_LENGTH and builds an array-element path for JSON_EXTRACT from the sequence value.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent order-item index report. A bounded sequence relation expands each order's item array, JSON_EXTRACT receives a zero-based path derived from the one-based sequence number, and empty arrays produce no rows; the source schema, names, values, and reporting purpose are not copied.

fixture_notes: Order 501 has three items, order 502 has one item, and order 503 has an empty array. The sequence join must emit exactly four indexed item rows and omit the empty order.
determinism_notes: Sequence values, JSON array order, zero-based path construction, and the final order-by keys are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE order_payloads (order_id INT PRIMARY KEY, payload JSON NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE item_sequence (seq_no INT PRIMARY KEY)

steps.sql: SELECT o.order_id, s.seq_no, JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(o.payload, CONCAT('$.items[', s.seq_no - 1, '].sku'))) AS sku, CAST(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(o.payload, CONCAT('$.items[', s.seq_no - 1, '].qty'))) AS UNSIGNED) AS quantity FROM order_payloads AS o JOIN item_sequence AS s ON s.seq_no <= JSON_LENGTH(o.payload, '$.items') ORDER BY o.order_id, s.seq_no
